first_impression.reaction: Okay, this is what I typed in. First line tells me it's 12 real couples sorted by setting, each linking to their story. That's exactly what I wanted, no pop-up, no waffle. I'd scroll down to the beach bit and probably tap one story.

journey.quote: Every Australia real wedding on this page comes from a story on our own pages: 12 couples, grouped by the setting they chose, whether that was a clifftop, a vineyard, a city room, a garden or an island.
journey.reaction: Straight answer in the first sentence. I know what's here and how it's sorted. Good.

journey.quote: Every wedding below comes from our own published stories, grouped by setting and linked to the couple's full account.
journey.reaction: This just repeats the intro. I'd rather the takeaways told me which settings there are so I can jump straight to one.

journey.quote: To marry legally in Australia, you give a Notice of Intended Marriage to an authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding.
journey.reaction: Not what I searched for, but it's short and specific. Fine to know, I'll skip past it.

journey.section: Real weddings by the coast and beach
journey.quote: In Wollongong, Jennifer and Emrah exchanged vows on a clifftop beside the beach before moving on to a glamorous reception. White, black and gold carried the theme from one to the other.
journey.reaction: Short, tells me the place and the look in two lines. This is the bit I'd actually read on the train, and I'd tap through.

journey.section: Real weddings by the coast and beach
journey.quote: They married on a spring afternoon.
journey.reaction: Spring of what year though? None of the stories say when they happened, so I can't tell if these are recent.

journey.quote: Four gardens, from the Adelaide Hills to private grounds in Victoria and a green garden near the Gold Coast.
journey.reaction: Says four, lists three. Small thing, but I noticed.

journey.quote: On a reef island, the water, the planting and the light arrive before a single flower is brought in.
journey.reaction: Bit flowery. Just tell me who married there.

journey.quote: Sunscreen goes on at least 20 minutes before heading outside, and again every two hours or after a swim or heavy sweating.
journey.reaction: I searched for real weddings, not sunscreen tips. By here I've already left or bookmarked.

journey.quote: Each card above links to the couple's full story, and our real weddings hub carries couples from Australia and beyond.
journey.reaction: Useful if I want more, and the headings are easy to scan.

unanswered_questions: When did these weddings take place? Are any of them recent?
Roughly what did any of these weddings cost? Just tell me a ballpark.
Which states are covered at a glance? I have to scroll each section to find out.

turn_offs_found.quote: Trees and built shade cut UV, yet some still reaches guests by reflection, so treat shade as one layer alongside covering clothing, hats, sunglasses and SPF 50 or SPF50+ sunscreen.
turn_offs_found.why: Long sun-safety detail on a page I came to for real wedding inspiration. Feels like padding, though it is far enough down that it doesn't block the answer.

turn_offs_found.quote: On a reef island, the water, the planting and the light arrive before a single flower is brought in.
turn_offs_found.why: Mood line instead of information. Slows the scan.

would_share_with: My fiance, if one of the stories matches what we like

cta_reaction.quote: Share with Wedded Concierge the setting you picture, the month you are weighing, your guest numbers and how far everyone will travel.
cta_reaction.why: I don't know this brand and I'm only browsing. I'd bookmark the page or open a story first. Nothing about the ask puts me off, I'm just not at that point yet.

top_3_changes: Make the first Key Takeaway list the five settings so I can jump straight to the one I care about, instead of repeating the intro.
Fix the garden intro so it names all four gardens it says it has, including the New South Wales one.
Swap the island mood line for a plain line saying who married there and in what kind of spot.

suggested_edits.old: - Every wedding below comes from our own published stories, grouped by setting and linked to the couple's full account.
suggested_edits.new: - Every wedding below comes from our own published stories: 12 couples grouped by coast, country and vineyard, city, garden and island, each linked to the couple's full account.
suggested_edits.why: Uses only what the intro and headings already say. Lets me scan the settings in the takeaways and jump.

suggested_edits.old: Four gardens, from the Adelaide Hills to private grounds in Victoria and a green garden near the Gold Coast.
suggested_edits.new: Four gardens, from the Adelaide Hills and formal grounds in New South Wales to private grounds in Victoria and a green garden near the Gold Coast.
suggested_edits.why: Intro said four but listed three. The New South Wales garden and its grounds are already described in the Paige and Todd card.

suggested_edits.old: On a reef island, the water, the planting and the light arrive before a single flower is brought in.
suggested_edits.new: One couple married on an island in the Whitsundays, in a courtyard ringed by tropical gardens.
suggested_edits.why: Plain information instead of a mood line, taken only from the Jessica and Jarrod card.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya, a phone reader from Google who doesn't know the brand
No invented brand facts; missing info listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and fact markers treated as invisible
Suggested edits add no prices, venue or vendor names, statistics, business details or new facts about the real weddings
No more than 3 suggested edits, each with an exact old string from the draft

assumptions: Image slots are HTML comments, so I judged the page as text only and did not mark down for missing or heavy images.
Read as Priya would: intro, Key Takeaways, one section of cards, then a skim of headings and the FAQ.

open_questions.question: Wedding dates and costs aren't on the page. Should the cards say when each wedding was published or held, if the source stories show it? I can't tell from here whether that information exists.
